minutes.headline: Marijuana bylaw (Art. 25) passed; all prohibitions failed to reach two-thirds; 3% excise tax and charter changes passed.
minutes.summary: Town Meeting spent most of its time on marijuana: Article 25 passed as amended after setback columns were changed to dashes, while prohibitions on cultivators, manufacturers, testing facilities and retailers failed to reach two-thirds. Later articles added a 3 percent excise tax, an anti-segmentation cluster bylaw, charter revisions and a solar PILOT, and rejected accepting a Whalum Road parcel.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed Article 25, the marijuana bylaw, as amended, by the required two-thirds.
Article 25 was amended first, with three setback columns changed to dashes, on a vote of 58 yes to 49 no as announced.
Every prohibition article on cultivators, manufacturers, testing facilities, retailers, transporters and researchers failed to reach two-thirds.
Article 32, accepting the excise tax on retail marijuana, passed; the Moderator noted three percent is the legal maximum.
Articles 33, 35 and 36 passed unanimously, Article 37 on a solar PILOT passed, and Article 34 on a Whalum Road parcel failed.

why_it_matters: Because the prohibitions failed, retail and other marijuana businesses can be sited under the Article 25 bylaw, and the excise tax gives the town budget, mostly taxes, a new local revenue source.
The solar PILOT sets a fixed payment in place of regular property tax on that project for twenty years, which affects what that property contributes to the tax base.
